description: 5 exemplars (one German) + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-10-14 under road-to-sentences-the-tree-can-back, whose step made this skill's market-size, growth-rate, price and competitor claims defer to a cited source — which brought the skill into check_routing_coverage's touched-skill scope. Exemplars cover the three entry points the skill's own 'When to use' names: a new market on the table across each of the three axes the Step 0 framing separates (geo, segment, vertical), a saturating market looking for the next growth window, and a regulatory shift that reopens the entry case. Near-misses are the three neighbours the skill's own 'Do NOT use' line names, each sharing its vocabulary and owned by somebody else: a capability gap to close by building or buying (build-buy-partner), a peer-versus-peer narrative (competitive-positioning, which this skill composes rather than replaces), and per-customer economics inside a market already entered (unit-economics-modeling). Counterexamples guard two homonyms this skill's own trigger words carry: 'entry' as a program entry point, and 'market data' as an exchange feed.

queries.q: we're US-only today and the board wants EU — should we enter, and where would we start?
we've sold SMB for three years and want to move upmarket — which segment first, SMB to mid-market or straight to enterprise?
our core market is saturating — which adjacent vertical actually unlocks the next growth window?
the new medical-device regulation just changed what we'd have to ship in healthcare — does that kill the entry case or make it?
lohnt sich der Markteintritt in APAC, und mit welchem Brückenkopf fangen wir an?
we lack a billing engine for the new region — do we build it, buy it, or partner?
queries.note: a capability gap inside the entry, not the entry decision → build-buy-partner

queries.q: how do we tell the story against the two incumbents who already own that segment?
queries.note: peer-versus-peer narrative; this skill composes it but does not own it → competitive-positioning

queries.q: what's our payback period per customer in the market we opened last year?
queries.note: economics inside a market already entered → unit-economics-modeling

queries.q: the CLI entry point is still src/index.ts — move it to bin/ and update the package manifest
queries.note: says entry, means a program entry point

queries.q: our market data feed from the exchange lags about forty seconds — where's the backpressure?
queries.note: says market, means an exchange price feed
